newsitem.title: UK: Matthew Clark up on bullish press report.
newsitem.headline: Matthew Clark up on bullish press report.

text.p: Shares in Matthew Clark, lingering near seven-year lows, jumped by almost 6.5 percent on Thursday after a press report suggested the stock is due for a recovery, dealers said.
By 1209 GMT, the shares were up 16-1/2p to 275-1/2.

The Times newspaper noted that shares in the UK cidermaker are trading on seven times this year's profits, or about half the average for the sector. The ratio, the report said, "suggests either that there is further trouble ahead, or that the City has overdone the fall."

The Times concluded, "the shares look a good two-way bet; if they stay at this level, a bid from one of the bigger drink groups attracted by well known brands such as Blackthorn cider looks inevitable. More likely, they will rebound once the City regains its nerve."
Some analysts are hopeful that Matthew Clark's half year figures, due January 14, may show that steps taken by management to reverse the company's collapse will work.

"There are a number of salesman out there pushing the stock saying the shares have come off enough and its time for a rebound. It's obviously a view not based on fundamentals but more a gut instinct," said one analyst close to the company.

Matthew Clark shook the market in September with a profits warning that wiped more than 290 million stg off its market value. Since then, the shares have held up at about 40 percent of the pre-warning level of 670p.
At the time, Matthew Clark said it planned to maintain its dividend at 9.0p for the half year ending October 31.
Brokers forecasts for pretax profits were slashed by about 30 percent since its September profit warning to some 45-50 million for the full year.
Smaller downward revisions have persisted amid continued uncertainty about the company's strategy and the actual mix of sales and prices achieved.
